claim.claim-text: 1. A wetting mechanism for wetting a tube of a catheter, the wetting mechanism comprising:

a housing configured to be positioned initially at or proximal to the tip end of the catheter tube, and wherein the housing comprises: a holding chamber for containing a volume of fluid therein; and a wetting chamber into which at least a portion of the catheter tube is able to be introduced and be moved therethrough to move at least a portion of the catheter tube through the wetting chamber, in use; and

wherein the wetting mechanism comprises a fluid release control component for controlling release of the fluid from the holding chamber to the wetting chamber, wherein the fluid release control component comprises a container of fluid positioned within the holding chamber, wherein the fluid release control component comprises a first configuration wherein it prevents release of the fluid from the holding chamber to the wetting chamber and the container is intact, having the fluid contained therein, wherein the fluid release control component comprises a second configuration wherein it allows release of the fluid from the holding chamber to the wetting chamber and the container has ruptured or has otherwise been opened to release fluid therefrom.
2. A wetting mechanism as claimed in claim 1 wherein the wetting mechanism is configured such that the container may be ruptured or otherwise opened, in use, through user action on the housing.

3. A wetting mechanism as claimed in claim 2 wherein the housing is formed at least partly from a flexible, compressible and/or resilient material, and the wetting mechanism is configured such that the container may be ruptured or otherwise opened upon a user compressing, bending and/or flexing the housing.

4. A wetting mechanism as claimed in any preceding claim, configured to be coupled to a sleeve, and configured such that fluid released into the wetting chamber is able to flow into and along a coupled sleeve to wet the catheter tube, in use.

5. A wetting mechanism of any preceding claim comprising a wetting applicator positioned within the wetting chamber configured to hold fluid released into the wetting chamber from the holding chamber.

6. A wetting mechanism of any preceding claim wherein the fluid release control component comprises a plug which is linearly moveable within the wetting mechanism between first and second positions corresponding to first and second configurations of the fluid release control component.

7. A wetting mechanism as claimed in claim 6 wherein the plug is configured to be at least partly withdrawn from the wetting mechanism to cause release of fluid from the holding chamber into the wetting chamber.
8. A wetting mechanism according to claim 6 or 7 configured such that the container is ruptured or otherwise opened, in use, through movement of the plug.
9. A wetting mechanism according to claim 8 configured such that the container is compressed upon at least partial withdrawal of the plug, or upon rotation of the plug.
10. A wetting mechanism according to any preceding claim wherein the container comprises one of a sachet, blister pack, or capsule.

11. A catheter, comprising: a catheter tube having a tip end and a distal end; and the wetting mechanism of any preceding claim operably coupled at or proximal to the tip end of the catheter tube for wetting the catheter tube, in use.
12. A catheter according to claim 11 which is a male urinary catheter.
13. A sealed packaged catheter according to claim 11 or claim 12, wherein the wetting mechanism is operably coupled at or proximal to the tip end of the catheter tube within the sealed package.
14. A method for wetting a tube of a catheter using the wetting mechanism of any of claims 1 to 10, the method comprising:

operating the fluid release control component to cause the release of fluid from the holding chamber into the wetting chamber; and introducing the tip end of the catheter tube into the wetting chamber and moving it therethrough, thereby wetting at least a portion of an outer surface of the catheter tube.
15. The method of claim 14 further comprising compressing, bending and/or flexing the housing to rupture or otherwise open the container.
